Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that quarantined content is retained but excluded from all retrieval results.
column7: Excluding quarantined content from all retrieval results is one way to contain poisoned RAG or memory content while it remains stored.
column8: Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-01. Exclusion is the enforced effect.

column2: Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that a swarm-level kill-switch exists that can halt all active agent instances.
column7: A swarm-level kill switch that halts all active agent instances is one way to contain an incident involving a runaway or compromised multi-agent system, letting responders perform containment manually (Ex2).
column8: Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-01. A kill switch is one containment technique among others.

column2: Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that policy violations trigger automatic containment of affected tools, such as stopping their execution, isolating them, or revoking their permissions.
column7: Automatically stopping, isolating or revoking permissions of tools that violate policy is one way for technology to perform containment actions automatically (Ex1) when agent tools are compromised or misbehave.
column8: Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-01. Manual containment would be an alternative.

column2: Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that a manual kill-switch mechanism exists to immediately halt AI model inference and outputs.
column7: A manual kill switch that immediately halts model inference and outputs is one way for responders to perform containment manually (Ex2) when an AI system is compromised or behaves harmfully.
column8: Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-01. A kill switch is one containment technique.

column2: Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that kill-switch commands are implemented through an out-of-band channel that is isolated from the agent runtime.
column7: Delivering kill-switch commands through an out-of-band channel isolated from the agent runtime is one way to keep containment actions available even when a compromised agent tries to disable in-band shutdown.
column8: Precedent: IR-4 -> RS.MI-01. The purpose is assured containment.

column2: Incidents are contained
column6: Verify that detection of suspected extraction triggers response measures.
column7: Triggering response measures such as throttling or blocking when model extraction is suspected is one way to contain an AI-specific incident.
column8: Matches RS.MI-01 Ex1 (automatic containment actions). Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-01.

column2: Incidents are eradicated
column6: Verify that memory can be reset.
column7: Providing the ability to reset AI memory is one way to let responders eradicate persistent memory poisoning (Ex2: responders select and perform eradication actions).
column8: Precedent: NIST maps SP 800-53 IR-4 to RS.MI-02. The main threat is persistent poisoning.

column2: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored
Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
column6: Verify that rollback capabilities restore the complete model state.
column7: A rollback capability that restores the complete model state (weights, configuration, adapters, safety models, prompts) is one way to restore AI systems to a known-good, consistent operating state.
column8: The requirement demands the restore capability, not backup creation. Redeploying from backups is an alternative means. Precedent: CP-10 -> RC.RP-05.
